newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. priest quits after Brazilians' sex charge.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. priest quits after Brazilians' sex charge.

text.p: The rector of a New York parish has resigned after the Episcopal Church began investigating a published report alleging priests brought young men from Brazil for sex, a church official said on Monday.

A story in December's issue of Penthouse magazine said a group of at least six gay and bisexual cross-dressing priests dressed up as movie stars such as Marilyn Monroe, called themselves "the girls" and staged orgies on the altar of St. Gabriel's Church in Brooklyn, New York.

Two Brazilian men were quoted by the magazine as saying that a 60-year-old rector, the Rev. William Lloyd Andries, had over the years brought young men from Brazil and other countries promising them jobs in the church.
The Bishop of the Diocese of Long Island to which St. Gabriel's belongs, the Right Rev. Orris Walker, said in a statement that Andries resigned last week.
"I am calling for an investigation of this most disturbing stituation by the Chancellor's Office and have accepted the resignation of Father Andries' orders, and thus, his rectorship," Walker said.
He said the Penthouse story "distressed me deeply" and that "it was imperative that we make every effort to determine the truth of the assertions to be found in this article."
The magazine said that the two Brazilians, who were the main sources for the story, were willing to cooperate with the investigation by Episcopal Church officials.
One of the men, Jairo Pereira, was photographed during a ceremony earlier this year at Andries' home during which Andries and Pereira "married," the magazine said.

It quoted the other Brazilian, 23-year-old Wasticlinio Barros, as saying that he had sex four to seven times a week with Andries or others of "the girls" in churches, church offices, cars and vans. Barros, who told Penthouse he was bisexual, alleged that Andries also regularly gave him cocaine, prescription drugs and alcohol.
The Episcopal Church, a Protestant denomination, is part of the Anglican Communion.
